utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: If I could remind you, General, of the affirmation you made at the beginning of your evidence, which still applies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Borovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: I am Borivoj Borovic and I represent Radic. My first question is: While you were in the Yugoslav army were you in favour of the concept of an independent Republic of Croatia?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: While I was in the Yugoslav People's Army I was for Yugoslavia. I was never in favour of an independent Republic of Croatia. I'm not that now. I am in favour of the Republic of Croatia, though, the way it is structured now.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: At the point in time when you decided to back such a state, Croatia was part of the common Socialist Federative Republic of Yugoslavia, is that true?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was a part of it. But it was already very close to a different concept of the order of the SFRY.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: When you moved to the Croatian side from the JNA, was the idea on the independence of that Croatian republic already formed?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean did I form that idea? Yes. I agreed with that concept September and wanted to assist with the implementation of that concept because the political structures which had been elected in Croatia had already, to a large part, conceived this idea and it was ripe.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. When was the first time that an independent Republic of Croatia was formed, independent state of Croatia was formed, can you help the Court?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you thinking of the NDH, the independent state of Croatia Nezavisna Drzava Hrvatska, the one that was formed in World War II?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, if you say it's the first time it was formed, then, yes.

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was its name. The first time it was formed, on the 10th of April 1941, and it was a state that is not referred to any more by anyone in Croatia and nobody holds that to be part of the positive foundations of the present Republic of Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Perhaps we could give some more information to the Chamber during World War II, an independent state of Croatia was formed, the NDH?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Independent state of Croatia which was formed in 1941 was inaugurated on the tanks of fascist Germany and Italy.

utterances.speaker: MR. AGHA
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would like to object to my learned friend's line of questioning because, although yesterday many of the questions had a political flavour, I believe, these questions have very much a historical flavour and I believe the witness, being a military witness, is really not in a position to deal with them adequately and perhaps they should be left to a historian.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Borovic, a slightly different question: What is the relevance of this history, so many years earlier, to the events in 1991?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, since I don't have a lot of questions on this topic, but this is directly linked with the newly formed independent state of Croatia, and what was happening to the Serbian people and what was in the consciousness of these people who were carrying out certain steps in order to protect themselves from things that were very similar to the things that already happened in 1941. This is the essence of why I am going into this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You may continue on that line, with the proviso that it is stretching relevance and so do not waste too much time on it, but also bearing in mind what Mr. Agha has very rightly pointed out, the Chamber will hear this evidence from the general, but without any expectation that he has any historical expertise so that he will simply be doing his best and if something is beyond his knowledge, he will undoubtedly indicate that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: As a soldier, did you hear that during World War II in the territory of Croatia, the largest concentration camp was established in that territory, named Jasenovac in the Balkans -- the largest concentration camp was established in the Balkans and it was named Jasenovac.

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I knew about it but I didn't know it was the largest one in the Balkans.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that between 700.000 and 1.2 million Serbs were killed there according to estimates that were made after the war?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have heard different figures. However, you mentioned the lowest one, which was historically disputed, and the number of casualties is much -- is actually much lower and this is something that was established by historians.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: The creators of that state, were they people whose military formations were called Ustasha military formations?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A number of the people who formed the state did have Ustasha military formations. However, there were other people whose formations were called SS units. And I also don't know what the Italian fascist forces were called in the territory of the former Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Does that mean that the Ustashas, the SS divisions, and Hitler's soldiers were allies in World War II?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Would you be kind enough to tell us what the flag, if you know, as a soldier, of that state looked like, the state from 1941 to 1945? What were the symbols on that flag?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, it was a red, white and blue flag, traditional Croatian flag, with a coat of arms. As it was -- as it was popularly called, "the chequerboard," but it was different than the flag of the modern Republic of Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: But the present modern state of Croatia also has the chequerboard on its flag?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The chequerboard is on the flag but it's different. The order of colours is different than the order during the NDH time and the historical coats of arms are different.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: What about the military insignia on the uniforms of Ustasha formation and formations of the ZNG? Are they similar or not?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what the insignia was in Ustasha formations.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And my last question on this topic, I'm going to take into account, of course, the suggestion of the Trial Chamber. Do you know who Andrija Artukovic was?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do. That was a man who was one of the ministers in the government of the NDH. After the war he fled the area and he was tried as a war criminal in Zagreb and was sentenced to a long prison sentence or a death sentence, I really cannot remember which one.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Was he held accountable for war crimes against the Serbian people?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was held to account for war crimes committed during the NDH under his leadership. I don't know against whom the war crimes were committed because there was also a large number of Croats who were casualties in a large number of camps throughout the former Yugoslavia as well as in Croatia, even though the largest number of casualties were Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we then agree, if I assert from the opinion of the Defence, that in order to prevent a repeat of the events from 1941, Serb people did have reason to take steps to protect themselves, including to seek protection from the JNA when their rights were jeopardised? Do you have an answer to that question?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That question was very topical as of 1989, as soon as the introduction of a multi-party system was announced on the territory of the former Yugoslavia. I tried to convince with a series of arguments my colleagues, which thought along those lines, and were afraid that some kind of system would be restored in which some of the peoples would be threatened. I hope that I managed to save a large number of people who did not opt to have a Croat system which would be against any particular people.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Your duties as chief of security of the 5th Corps, that was your -- one of your posts; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Was one of your duties to protect from terrorist activities?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: In view of the duties that you were performing, do you know when anti-terrorist, anti-sabotage units were formed in the army of Yugoslavia? What year was that?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's been ten, 15 or 20 years when that was done. There were no such units in the air force so I was not responsible for them, but I know that they were thinking along those lines after there were hijackings of planes internationally, also after the incursion in 1972 of a group.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Excuse me, I think it was 1974. Are you thinking of Radusa?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, it was 1972 but if you say it was 74, very well. So sometime in that area, they considered the formation of such units.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I apologise for interrupting you. My question actually was the following: In 1974, in a place called Radusa was there an incursion by a Ustasha sabotage unit into Croatia?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, there is no such place.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Radusa?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Would you be kind enough to tell us what was the place where the Ustasha units came for the first time?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These were not Ustasha units. It was a so-called terrorist/sabotage unit which entered the territory of the SFRY near Maribor, near Gornja Radgona, they crossed the road and made it to Bugojno not to mountain Radusa. There was no place called Radusa.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much so would you agree that it was an Ustasha sabotage group and that the incursion of that group was the cause or the reason why the JNA formed these anti-sabotage, anti-terrorist units?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was not the first group that entered the territory of Yugoslavia. Since 1945, throughout history, there were more such groups. It's possible that this is one of the reasons but I don't know if it's the main reason.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. Did you hear of a person called Miro Baresic?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have heard of him.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: It's not in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I've heard of him.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Would you tell the Trial Chamber who that is?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is a member of an emigre organisation in the west. It was abroad. He moved through a large number of countries in the west.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In 1991, he was killed in Lika, under circumstances which have still not been clarified.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: So you say he was a member of an emigre organisation. Which emigre organisation?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was a member of a Croatian emigre organisation but I don't know what was the name of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Since you have information that he was killed in 1992, my question is: Was he killed as a member of a Croat paramilitary organisation in the area or was he perhaps a member of some other formation that was in the territory of Croatia?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was killed in 1991, sometime in the summer of 1991, in the area of Ravni Kotari. As a member of the reserves -- reserve forces of the Ministry of Internal Affairs. As far as I know he was not under my command.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Members of the reserve forces of the Ministry of Internal Affairs, were they not, according to your replies, also members of the ZNG?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A large number of the ZNG members were part of the same from the ranks of the reserve forces of the MUP, the Ministry of Internal Affairs of the Republic of Croatia, but not all of them. You could say that a smaller number became members of the ZNG.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And would you agree with my information that Miro Baresic was a Croatian Ustasha and that he killed the ambassador of the Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia named Rolovic? Do you know about that incident, that case?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know if he was a Ustasha because the Ustashas in 1945 were vanquished and so there were none of those later on. But that he referred to the -- whether he referred to the Ustasha movement or was sympathetic with it, I don't know. He was a younger man born after the war, and as far as I know, from the information we received in the service, that went round the service, he was one of the people involved in the assassination of Ambassador Rolovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: And do you know about the fact that he was proclaimed a member of the international terrorist organisation after that and that an international wanted poster was issued for him? He was wanted internationally?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, after every killing, the perpetrators are sought and wanted. Miro Baresic as far as I remember, was tried in Sweden, I believe, and so he did -- was held accountable for his crime.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. AGHA
utterances.text: Your Honours, I apologise for interrupting my learned friend but I'm wondering what the relevance are of these questions regarding the actual indictment which concerns a very limited crime of the alleged murder of 200-odd people from a hospital.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Agha, as we have indicated on occasion so far, the Prosecution undoubtedly has one view of what is relevant to this offence or these offences, the Defence a different one. The Chamber has to allow to both sides some reasonable opportunity to present the case as they see it. If something is evidently not relevant, certainly we will intervene. At the moment, this area of discussion, at least insofar as it deals with events in 1991, is not one which the Chamber is able to rule out as not relevant. So you will understand that we fully appreciate that it is not what you see to be relevant but I suspect that your ideas and Mr. Borovic's would be quite apart on the issue. So please carry on, Mr. Borovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Agotic, you said yesterday when asked by my colleague, Mr. Vasic, a question, that in Croatia in the period in 1991, the Yugoslav People's Army was considered the occupation army; is that right, an occupying force, that that's how they were viewed?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Do you know when the Yugoslav People's Army was established and when it set foot on -- in Vukovar for the first time and when the barracks were attacked? Do you know what year that was?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: All right. Very well. How can you explain to us then the fact that all the barracks of the Yugoslav People's Army and all the men in those barracks were on the territory of Croatia and how was it that they according to you they could suddenly become an occupying force, an occupational army? So what triggered this off and who proclaimed, suddenly proclaimed the Yugoslav People's Army to be an enemy army when it had been there for 50 years?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Yugoslav People's Army on the territory of Croatia was not proclaimed by the Croatian leadership an occupying force, but it was the army which took sides in the conflict that broke out on the territory of the former Yugoslavia, and it took one side, in actual fact, a long time ago. Or we could almost say before the armed conflicts actually broke out and the barricades were erected on the territory of Croatia. And if I might be allowed to add, and if you're interested in hearing, I can also tell you that the chief of the General Staff in June 1990, that is to say not 15 days after the Croatian authorities were elected at democratic elections, and we must bear that in mind all the time, that they were democratic elections and whether the Chief of Staff, Colonel General Adzic, before a large number of officers, high-ranking army officers at the Pleso airport, when asked by one of the generals present, a JNA general present, he was asked -- they asked him, "How are we going to cooperate, General, with the new Croatian authorities?" Because up until now, we had very good relations with the structures in power and the people on the territory of Croatia. General Adzic's answer was this: He said, "I have no cooperation with Tudjman. Tudjman should be said get out of that seat, get out of your chair." So that was the programme of the Yugoslav People's Army vis-a-vis the Croatian authorities and powers that be.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. May I make a comment and say that Tudjman at that time advocated a pure nationalistic programme, that is to say a programme by virtue of its goals represented in fact a programme pursued by the NDH, the independent state of Croatia, dating back to 1941.

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you have every right to your opinion but I'm quite certain that that is not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: All right. Never mind. We don't want to enter into the realms of politics. I will respect the guidelines given by the Chamber and stop there. But I do have to ask you this: Were you ever a communist yourself?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, from 1963 until the end of 1990.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: And after that, were you a member of the HDZ, the Croatian party?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not a member of any party afterwards, after the League of Communists of Yugoslavia was abolished which was the 15th of January 1991 or thereabouts, when all the officers of the former JNA were asked to state their views whether they were in favour of the League of Communists of Yugoslavia or not. And I said I was not and I have remained non-party-affiliated to the present day.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: I see. Did you personally or indirectly take part in struggles against members of the Yugoslav People's Army, not former Yugoslav People's Army but the Yugoslav army?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I took part indirectly because I was in charge of the structures that organised defence, defence from the Yugoslav People's Army and from anybody who wanted to launch an attack on Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, you also -- you said indirectly. How many times did you command the attack on the barracks of the Yugoslav People's Army, command operations of attacks against the barracks of the Yugoslav People's Army, for instance?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not once. I was never in command of anything like that because that was the position of the political leadership of the Republic of Croatia whereby the barracks should be blocked, and then in the second stage the warehouses, that the warehouses should be taken over to arm Croatia and to take control of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Yesterday you mentioned the example of the Bjelovar barracks and directly asked by my colleague Mr. Vasic, you said that you had heard that the commander of the barracks in Bjelovar was killed or rather taken -- my question to you is after he was arrested by the Croatian National Guards Corps was he liquidated, was he executed? That's a direct question.

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know if owe was executed but I do know that an investigation was conducted after the Bjelovar barracks had been taken over and that individuals were held responsible before the Croatian courts.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Now, is the following piece of information correct, that during the blockades and during the time when the barracks were seized from the Yugoslav People's Army it was under your direct command that 36 soldiers of the Yugoslav People's Army were killed? Is that correct? Is that true?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know how many soldiers were killed but that there were casualties on both sides, a relatively large number of casualties, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And how many casualties on the other side would you say there were?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't say how many casualties there were on the Croatian side. I know there were quite a lot, especially among the civilian population in towns.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. As the commander of the Croatian National Guards Corps, the ZNG, did you receive the following information: Do you know how many foreign nationals were members of the Croatian National Guards Corps?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have that information to hand but I do know that some foreign citizens were among the ranks of the Croatian army and a smaller portion in the ZNG as well. But in the Croatian army, there were indeed perhaps several hundred, a couple of hundred.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Do you know which countries they came from, those mercenaries?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all they were not mercenaries because everybody was paid in the Croatian army, everybody received a salary if they were in the Croatian army. But they would come in for the same salaries, sometimes even for foregoing their salaries, from England, from Holland, from America, from Argentina, from Australia, from a large number of countries, in fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know whether there were any such foreign nationals in the ZNG Corps in Vukovar in 1991?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know whether there were any amongst the defenders of Vukovar. However, a large number of Croats in the foreign legion came in to defend the country and, amongst other things, Vukovar, too.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, do you know how they joined the Croatian National Guards Corps, since you were the commander -- a commander and they belonged to the foreign legion, what was the procedure for membership? Could you explain that to us a little, please?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the procedure wasn't very complicated. If you wanted to join up with the National Guards Corps, you had to state your decision to fight for the defence of Croatia and you would have to contact the Ministry of the Interior. They had their personnel department. And contracts would be signed, agreements reached, with the members joining up with the international guards and they would receive a regular monthly salary.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Do you know how high that salary was?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As a colonel of the former JNA, since my rank was acknowledged and recognised although we didn't have ranks afterwards, my first salary was somewhere in the region of 30 to 32.000 dinars. The then Yugoslav dinars.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: And what about these people from the foreign legion that joined up with the ZNG? What were their salaries?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, our salaries were the same. I don't think there were any differences.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So at the time, on the territory which belonged to an area where these war events were taking place, in Vukovar, we had members of the Croatian National Guards Corps; is that right?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Vukovar itself, a very small number, but yes, there were members of the ZNG.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: And members of the MUP of Croatia?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Any HOS members?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that in Vukovar itself, there weren't any HOS members but in the defence of Vukovar, indirectly, along the front lines there were members of the HOS.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: And what were the names of the members of the paramilitary formations and units - you told us something about that - that were led by Mercep?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were the defenders of Vukovar, organised by the Secretariat for National Defence of the Vukovar municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Did they not have a separate name?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know they didn't. Perhaps he had a name for them or somebody calls them by some special name but they had no different official name except to be called the defenders of Vukovar.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, in Mercep's units, were the members mostly Croats, the majority were Croats, were they?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the majority were Croats although there were people of different ethnicities.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: And what conclusions can we make here in court, if we have a short sketch of this conflict where on the one side we have members of the MUP of Croatia and the Croatian National Guards Corps, members of the HOS, Mercep's volunteers, and on the other side, on the other hand, you just have the representatives of the Serb people who had not been militarily organised and established? What comment can you make? Did somebody need to help them out perhaps? Did they need assistance? To be quite specific, did they need the assistance of the Yugoslav People's Army? To be quite specific, to deal with this enormous military force which numbered a very many units as you've just told us here in court?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. They did not need any assistance because those who were organised to defend Croatia were not organised in order to take over these people in Croatia or to expel them.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know that the Prime Minister was in Vukovar in August 1991, in August 1991?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of what government?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: The Croatian government.

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about that. I'm not aware of that, but I think that Dr. Franjo Greguric was in Vukovar once while you were still able to enter.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Do you know the reason for the Prime Minister of the Croatian government to go to Vukovar, a town that was in that status?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the Prime Minister can move around the entire territory of his country, and I can tell you that Prime Minister Greguric was the president of the coalition government which was comprised of all the parties in the Sabor, or Croatian assembly, including Serb ministers, Serbs from Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know whether during that period of time, Franjo Tudjman visited Vukovar at all?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think he did during August and later certainly not.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I think he visited it in July, according to my information, but if you're not aware much that, let's move on. Do you know or are you aware of the fact that in Vukovar, from August until the end of November, so from August to the end of November is the period we are looking at, there were special permits that were in force which were issued by Mercep which prohibited free movement of citizens around the town of Vukovar or, more exactly, permits without which nobody was able to enter or to leave Vukovar? Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I was not aware of that. I didn't know that that was the manner in which he regulated the question of movement around Vukovar.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, if I tell you that the director of the hospital and the employees of the hospital confirmed the fact that these permits did in fact exist, were in existence, may I have your comments as to who could have given permission for permits like this to exist when the Croatian National Guards Corps existed, when MUP existed? Who could have given Martic [as interpreted] the go ahead to limit movement of the population in Vukovar in that way? Who could have given him that authority?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If that is true, that that was so, then I think he could have organised it himself.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction, Mercep was the name.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He organised defence. Now, how he could have done that I answered that yesterday and said that it was no pleasure doing that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, Your Honour, it seems that transcript reads Martic, instead of Mercep. Line 11, page 18. Could this please be corrected? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Did you hear of the 204th Vukovar Brigade?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Yesterday you didn't enumerate it when you gave testimony about brigades. Can you tell us what was the composition of this brigade? What was its area of responsibility, and what can you tell us about it?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 204th Brigade of Vukovar, or the 104th -- or the 124th Brigade, which is still in existence, it was never lined up as a brigade. And in order for it to acquire the status of brigade and the status of defenders of the town, it was ordered by the commander of the operations zone, the then colonel and later General Karl Gorinsek, to establish a brigade. The Main Staff gave one numeric denomination and he gave another one, and this is why this brigade is known under two names or two numbers. I didn't enumerate it because, as a brigade, neither then nor now was it in existence as a brigade of the town of Vukovar. This is why I didn't include it as a brigade. I said that the defenders of Vukovar were those who were an active factor in the defence of Vukovar.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: All right. But we didn't hear what was its area of responsibility and action. In which area was it active? Do you know that? And was it a brigade of the ZNG regardless of the fact whether it had a status of a brigade or not?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It was a brigade of the Croatian army which comprised defenders of Vukovar, meaning that all of those who defended Vukovar later on were included into the 204th or 124th brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: All right. Can you then explain to us, you have just referred to this force as the "Croatian army," and I think that your explanation was not quite a convincing one. Can you please tell us why, in 2003, the Croatian government legalised that status as late as 2003, if it was according to you a legal Croatian force? Why would the government legalise it only in 2003?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please do not assess my answers as convincing or not. It is up to the Trial Chamber to do that. Our job here is to establish the truth and this is why I tried to give very fair and accurate answers and I ask that you have the same attitude. 204th Vukovar Brigade was never established as such. In order for the status of Vukovar defenders to be legally regulated, they had to be listed as members of a brigade or a unit. This is why it wasn't done until 2003, and I believe that their status has not been finally legalised until to date.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: All right. Can we then conclude that the 204th Vukovar Brigade at that time was a paramilitary formation because it had no legal status, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Since your answer was no, would you please explain it?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told you that the task of those setting up the 204th brigade was to defend Vukovar.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: All right. So the defenders of Vukovar, can they attribute a status to a formation or is it something that is done by somebody at the level of the republic or higher level? Can any group of people attribute a status to a military formation in any modern country?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This is done by the Minister of Defence and the Main Staff. This is why I said that in 1991, sometime in October when they started establishing brigades in the Croatian army outside of the ZNG, I told you yesterday that there were four and later seven ZNG brigades, whereas all other brigades were brigades of the Croatian army. It was then that they started establishing them. However, the Vukovar Brigade in the administrative sense was not -- its status was not legally finalised until much later.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: All right. The situation is quite clear to me. And it is up to the Trial Chamber to judge. My next question is do you know who Marin Vidic, Bili, was?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Marin Vidic, Bili, yes, I know who he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Would you be so kind and tell us what you know about him?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Marin Vidic, Bili, was the commissioner of the government of the Republic of Croatia for the municipality of Vukovar. By occupation he's an engineer of agriculture and until then he had lived in a village. I believe the flame of the village was Lovas.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Do you know what authorities he had as a government commissioner in Vukovar during combat activities?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of all of his authorities but I know that presidents of municipalities and government commissioners were at the same time chiefs of staffs, Crisis Staffs, in that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: All right. At the time when you joined the ZNG and headed it, can you tell us who were the members of the Crisis Staff in Vukovar?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know the members but I know that the Crisis Staff was headed by the government commissioner for Vukovar.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: And by saying so, you mean precisely the person we just mentioned?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Do you know whether in that Crisis Staff, there was also the director of the Vukovar Hospital, during that period of time?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that. But I know that there was a director of the hospital who cooperated very closely with the government commissioner for Vukovar municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Since I'm not aware of that, of this type of cooperation, would you please explain what do you mean by close cooperation?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In view of the existing circumstances, the hospital had special needs. It needed all kinds of supplies. It needed to be protected. At the request of the director of the hospital, this was implemented on a priority basis by those who were in power, and in this case, it was the government commissioner for the municipality of Vukovar. He was the one authorised to do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Do you know who guarded the hospital? Was it the members of the ZNG or the MUP? Was it the volunteers or members of the Croatian army or members of the paramilitary units among whom you included HOS? Who guarded the hospital?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know who guarded the hospital during that period of time. Most likely some kind of defence units established at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: So it seems that you don't know.

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Did you hear of Dr. Njavro?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Was he a member of the ZNG?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Do you know whether he was a member of the reserve police forces of Croatia?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't believe he was. He was a physician and they were not militarily organised except military doctors.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. I think that we have information concerning what I'm about to ask you. Did you appoint Mile Dedakovic known as Jastreb and Branko Borkovic to take over the ZNG members in Vukovar?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I did instruct them to do that but not to take over the ZNG members, but rather to assume the leadership of the defence of Vukovar.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: So the jurisdiction that they have, what forces did they have jurisdiction over?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All forces who defended Vukovar.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Does that mean that they did not have under their command only the ZNG but also the policemen, members of HOS, Mercep's men, units of volunteers, as you called them, and so on?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said, I don't think that HOS members were present in Vukovar.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: But had they been, would they also be under their command?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Whoever was armed and was involved in defence of Vukovar came under the command of Mile Dedakovic, Jastreb, who was appointed to that post.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I think that you gave testimony about the members of the ZNG who were actually members of the MUP of Croatia. Does that mean that, by saying so, you are putting the MUP of Croatia under your control whereas formerly you were stating that you were under the MUP of Croatia?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The ZNG members were not under the MUP of Croatia. However, for administrative purposes, for salaries and for health protection and retirement insurance and so on, they were put on the records of the MUP of Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: To tell you the truth, I don't quite understand this. It seems that this was some kind of an administrative manipulation. They were not members of the MUP of Croatia, however they were on their payrolls and were established as a separate, independent formation. Can you explain this clearer, please?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Members of the ZNG from the 28th of May 1991 were within the composition of the Ministry of the Interior of Croatia as an independent armed formation. In addition to that, the Ministry of the Interior had reserve forces of police and regular police force, which had some 20.000 members. Additionally, MUP also had the state security service within it. So those were the organisation that is existed within the then MUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: All right. So when the time comes for the members of the ZNG to have all those units under their command, was it done pursuant to your order or an order of somebody above you?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I proposed the head of the defence of Vukovar, and the order was signed by the Supreme Commander of Croatia, to have him appointed as head of the Vukovar defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. One of the witnesses here told us that the commissioner in addition to all other authorities and tasks, was authorised to cut off water supply, electrical supply, to control all of those needs that existed in the town of Vukovar. Do you have any such information namely that he was authorised to have all of that under his control in Vukovar?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what kind of authorities he had. However, I know that the Crisis Staffs in the territory of the Republic of Croatia regulated those issues for the entire area.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: So that means that that fell under the jurisdiction of Crisis Staffs of all towns, including Vukovar?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Most likely that's how it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Does this mean that this issue as well fell within the responsibility of Marin Vidic, Bili, who was the chief of the Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Most likely that's how it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: In the towns that I mentioned to you, the barracks that had been blocked and taken away, seized from the JNA, all of these things is something that you have knowledge about. Was the electricity cut off to those barracks such as, for example, the one in Bjelovar, before the barracks were attacked? Was the electricity and water cut off?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Electricity, water supplies, and egress was controlled. This is what we called the blockade.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Was the same system applied in Vukovar even though during that period of time you your self were not in charge but do you know about the system? Was this system applied in Vukovar as well?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that Vukovar was a bit of a special case in view of the location of the barracks in Vukovar. I didn't visit the barracks until after the war, after the peaceful integration, and I think that I saw that this barracks was impossible to put under siege. The barracks in Vukovar was not especially important. It wasn't particularly large.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: I didn't mean the cases in Gospic, Bjelovar and so on but what I had in mind were the cutoffs of electricity, water and so on?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If the Crisis Staff was able to implement that, then, yes, the same system would be applied in Vukovar as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Does that mean that they -- the people in the barracks could not have turned off water and electricity for the hospital? It had to be done somewhere else?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know how the supply system is regulated Vukovar.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Trust me. I know that it is impossible to do it from the barracks in Vukovar. Yesterday you spoke about the Spegelj affair and I wouldn't like to go back to it now. Did you say how long after this operation -- did you say how many -- how many Kalashnikovs there were in the ZNG?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yesterday I replied that there is information indicating that about 40.000 Kalashnikovs were imported in that Spegelj operation. When the ZNG was established, there were somewhere about 8.000 Kalashnikovs.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: All right. In order not to repeat what was said yesterday, I will stop here. I will ask you something else. Did you personally ever propose to Tudjman to buy weapons?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In August of 1991, I briefed him and told him that we had many more people than we were able to arm.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Was that the period of time when there was an embargo on importing and procuring weapons? Was it during that period of time?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was immediately prior to the introduction of the arms embargo. It was introduced on the 1st of September 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Yesterday you said that during the embargo, you managed to procure weapons?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that during the embargo, we armed the Croatian army from the JNA barracks and depots.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Did you procure weapons from Hungary during that period of time?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can tell you that the members of the defence department were in charge of procuring weapons and equipment. I know that in the units most of the weapons originated from the JNA.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In response to a question by my learned friend Mr. Vasic, you said that when weapons of the Territorial Defence were blocked by the Yugoslav People's Army, you felt that they had seized the weapons, that it wasn't theirs, that it belonged to someone else and that that was how you treated that. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: If now members of the ZNG seize weapons from barracks belonging to the JNA, how would you call that? Would you call that illegal procurement of weapons? Is that seizing somebody else's property? What do you say to that?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I say that that would be taking your own property, which was also financed by Croatia within the former SFRY. It was in the situation of having to defend them -- itself. There was no way of obtaining weapons and it was the only way to get them. The other way would be to just go to church and to pray.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: My assessment is that it would have been better for you to have gone to church and prayed than to have seized weapons. But I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I apologise for making a personal comment.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: These weapons that were in the barracks of the JNA, did they belong to the peoples of other republics? Was that their property also?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the distribution ratio, you could see that Croatia owned 20 per cent of all JNA property.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: So that means that you had taken more than your fair share?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We did not take 20 per cent, and, as I said, actually, we were owed 27 per cent.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Well, we will leave that up to the Court. I'm going to cut this short so that we will be able to go on time for our first break. We looked at Exhibit 84 relating to the village of Bruska and then you mentioned in the remarks, and this was something that was on the ELMO for a long time, you said that there was a mistake there and that it stated there that not all Croats were Ustashas. Is that what it says?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It doesn't say that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell me what it says, then?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The comment by the major is that an investigation needed to be carried out again in order to take away the stigma from the Serbian people.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: So the investigation needed to be conducted again?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Because this has been admitted as an exhibit, and there were several comments, you noted at the end that the Croat people were not mentioned there at all, but what was mentioned were member of a sabotage unit of Ustashas who allegedly committed that crime. Why did you comment that that referred to the entire Croatian people?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Borovic, we are talking about different documents. The document that I commented on refutes the -- or the security organ refutes the assessment by the public security station or the police station in Benkovac, that the massacre was not carried out against the Marinkovics in the Bruska village by members of the terrorist sabotage group but that the massacre was a result of a quarrel dating back a few years ago with a family from some village that is mentioned and that they used this opportunity and committed a massacre against these nine people. So it was noted that this was not an act by an Ustasha sabotage terrorist unit but that it was a fight amongst people. They happened to be Serbs in this case so I believe that my comment was quite correct, the comment that I made at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: There is also Exhibit 85, that is the next document, where Pupovac and Skoric are mentioned as persons suspected of having committed the massacre; is that correct? Do you know what happened ultimately with Skoric and Pupovac? Were they tried, convicted? How did this case end?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. But it states there that the police officer - I think his name is Mladenovic - would know best who actually committed the massacre and this police officer was transferred to Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. If I were to tell you that on the 4th of November 2003, this is on page 28521, lines 9 to 12, a witness stated in the case of Slobodan Milosevic the following: "It does need to be remembered that one of the biggest ethnic cleansing in the whole of the Balkans during this period was that involving Serbs who had to flee Krajina in the early summer of 1995. The name of the witness is Lord David Owen." My question is: I have this transcript from the Milosevic case in English. If necessary, I can furnish that to the Prosecution but this is exactly what the witness said. What would be your comment about the events relating to the so-called Storm? Did you participate in Storm and in general what is your position in relation to that?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Storm operation -- before the operation I was a commander of the Croatian air force which was actively participating in the Operation Storm. I think that Operation Storm was an operation by the Croatian army which liberated territories occupied until that time. This was some 30 per cent of the territory. And that it was implemented in a very professional and proper manner, Operation Storm as such.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Does that mean that the witness, Lord David Owen, who testified in the case of Slobodan Milosevic --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Borovic, how is this relevant to events in 1991?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. It's relevant precisely because the witness directly participated in these events. He was chief of the Croatian army air force, and it's relevant as it relates to his credibility as someone who is personally interested in explaining the events from his own point of view, because the position of the Defence - and may the witness excuse me - is that there are witness -- witnesses to the event in which the witness was a commander. These witnesses refer to that event as ethnic cleansing. If at the time he was the commander of the air force, at the time when 300.000 people were expelled from Croatia, and some witnesses stated that this was a matter of ethnic cleansing, then we are proofing the position of the witness as it relates to the ZNG and the Croatian army, because we heard the witness say that this was a legal operation, that it was a brilliant military operation. Then that is the position of the witness in relation to events in 1991.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Borovic, the Chamber sees no sufficient relevance in events so many years after to the activities and the events of 1991, the subject of the indictment. So if you would leave that topic alone, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I think that actually these questions would suffice. I have one more question and then it will be, I think, time for the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Sir, as somebody who commanded the air force, did you participate in military operations in Bosnia outside the borders of Croatia?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I personally did not, but helicopters of the Croatian air force made more than 100 sorties, transporter choppers flew over 100 flights to Bosnia in order to evacuate the sick and the wounded.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: And was there any transfer of -- or transport of weapons?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. There was no transport of weapons, but only the transport of medical supplies. And if there was room, also food was carried.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Your Honour. It is time for a break and I would also like to inform you that I have no further questions for this witness. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Borovic. We could actually run for another quarter of an hour, Mr. Lukic. Would that suit you? We see you champing at the bit.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honours. Good afternoon to all the parties.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Agotic. I am Novak Lukic and I am representing Mr. Sljivancanin. I will be asking some questions now. The interpreters keep telling me off all the time that I talk very fast, so I'm going to try to respect also their request and also, as Mr. Vasic earlier said, please make a pause before you begin answering my questions in order to give the interpreters a chance to complete their interpretation. I heard from your CV that you are -- you have a masters in political sciences?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I would like to know what was the topic of your thesis and when did you graduate?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I graduated in the -- in early 1985, and my topic was non-alignment as a factor of security and efficacy of the defence of the SFRY.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: From your testimony yesterday, and also on Friday, I understood that you were assistant chief of security at the 5th Air Force Corps, already in 1974; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And that you became the chief and spent six years there, from 1985 until March 1991?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That is it, more or less.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I assume that in those five years, that you spent as chief and having in mind that for a long time before that you were in the same sector, in the same service, you were able to form a clear picture of your service and your section in that period.

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I was able to form a clear picture.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I would like to check one thing in respect of a question posed yesterday. Am I wrong when I say - and perhaps you didn't answer properly or, if you did, then it's my mistake - that you, as chief of the 5th Corps security service, were directly subordinated to the chief of the air force headquartered in Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. The headquarters were in Zemun.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And according to the command chain of command, you were subordinated to the commander of the 5th Air Force Corps?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yesterday and during the examination-in-chief and also through the transcript from the Milosevic case, this was recorded, and also in your answers given to my learned friend Mr. Vasic but still I would like to double-check. You said that the authority of the security service, as it relates to the security services at the JNA command, were regulated according to the rules of service of the armed forces of the SFRY adopted in 1984, according to the information that I have, and these authorities of the security service - and now I will refer to the testimony of the Prosecution military expert - were limited to expert or technical matters, according to Article 57 and 58 of the rules of service?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know exactly which articles they were but that's how it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Well, I don't want to read the regulations. The Trial Chamber will be able to learn about this when we call the military experts. I also assume that you are quite familiar with the first item or article of these rules. I am only briefly going to read that regulation or a part of the regulation. It's quite a large paragraph. "The organs of security, as expert organs, carry out state security tasks, amongst other things in order to uncover and prevent activities aimed at undermining or toppling the constitution of the SFRY, the social system, and aimed at threatening the security of the country, if such activities are carried out within the armed forces or against the armed forces from within the country or from abroad, and also in order to prevent activities aimed at violating the confidentiality and secrecy of tasks and assignments of the JNA." I think that this was also in force in the time period encompassed by the indictment. In order for the Chamber to be quite clear about this, and I believe that they are already quite informed about this question, but what or who comprised the armed forces of the SFRY at the time?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were comprised of land forces, the air force and anti-aircraft defence service, as well as the navy. These were the Yugoslav People's Army and Territorial Defence, organised in each republic and province.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: One answer that you gave to Mr. Borovic prompts me, in relation to this information that he sought regarding the emigre groups. You said that as part of the service, and that's how I understood it, you received information also about the activities of these emigre forces in relation to the killing of ambassador Rolovic in Oslo. That is what you said. My question is was this one of the tasks of the service to inform itself about external and not only internal things that are relevant for the defence of the country?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But first of all, about those elements which may endanger the security of the JNA or the unit in which the security organs were working.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This information that was sent, that is sent by the authorised organ in accordance with the hierarchy of the security organs or the security administration, was this something that acted as a kind of directive in the work of the security organ?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. They formed directives, guiding the work of such organs.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I gain the impression that you were well informed about the Vukovar battlefield from the moment I assume that you were given the assignment of organising the individuals who were to be sent to command these towns' defence. When did you actually send Dedakovic or Borkovic, or rather whether you've already given us the answer I apologise for asking you again but I don't think I heard your answer when did you propose that Dedakovic and Borkovic be sent to Vukovar?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that that was on the 28th of August 1991 or a day or two after that date.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And to the best of your knowledge, when did they actually leave? When did they go there?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we could say that it was on the 30th of August, that they arrived in Vukovar on the 30th of August and reported perhaps on the 1st of September. But that's give or take a day or two, just a day or two's difference.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I asked you when you made the proposal to Tudjman but you answered the question, so there is no doubt about him giving permission to your proposal; is that right?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Does the name Ante Aric ring a bell at all?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ante Aric, that's the first time I've heard of that name. Perhaps you've got the surname wrong? I know Ante Karic, perhaps, if that's who you meant.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Was he in Vukovar perhaps?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you receive feedback information from Dedakovic, Borkovic, with respect to the Vukovar operations and, if so, how frequently?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did receive information. They would call up on the phone to report on the situation, and to ask for assistance, more or less, in the form of manpower, equipment, later on medicines and so on, but no written reporting, no written reports.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: How often, if you can tell us roughly?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, approximately sometimes twice a day, sometimes once in three days, depending on how often they were able to report. But Vukovar wasn't the only problem and I was taken up with various affairs but roughly speaking that would be it. That would be the intensity of the reporting.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you have any direct information about the fact that Dedakovic talked directly to Tus and to Tudjman and that he asked them to send weapons first of all ammunition for heavy weapons, the 120 calibre and 158 calibre, millimetre calibre, do you know anything about that?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that he contacted a number of people, certainly General Tus and certainly the president of the country. Now what he asked for specifically, I really can't say. I don't know. But that he had need of ammunition and weapons, that is quite certain.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you -- he ask for NORA?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that he asked for artillery support from the units that were in the encirclement of Vukovar. He asked for tanks, too. However, we were not able to give him those things. So I don't know what -- he asked for -- everything that could help him in the defence of Vukovar would have been welcome.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I think we are going to take a break but my last question before we do so: Could you tell us what the NORAs are, what are NORAs?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They are heavy howitzers, as far as I know. I am not very well-versed in artillery, the people from the land forces would know that better than me. But it is a sophisticated, very modern type of weapon, howitzer, long range, solid-calibre weapon, very precise, high precision weapon but I don't know the details, the NORAs. Ask me about planes. I will tell you that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May we take a break now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Lukic. We will resume at ten minutes past four.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, I don't know whether the interpreters managed to get to you in the break, but I did notice that you are quite right when you say you speak quickly, and it would, I think, help them a great deal if you yourself paused after an answer, before asking the next question, and so forth. I'll give Mr. Borovic a coaching lesson next time.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I've been here for four years now, at the Tribunal, and I still haven't managed to learn. I've been hearing those criticisms for four years.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Agotic, I'll continue from where we left off and I was asking you some questions about information and whether you received feedback information from Dedakovic and Borkovic, in fact. Now, tell me this, please: Was it your idea and where do you get information about Dedakovic and Borkovic as people who you wished to commend for the defence of Vukovar? Did you know them previously or did you receive any recommendations to that effect?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew both Dedakovic and Borkovic from before, especially Dedakovic. Both of them were from the air force, air force men, that is to say corps units. Dedakovic, for a year or more, went to the 5th Military District from the 5th Corps. A year or more ahead. And when he was placed at our disposal, having left the JNA service, sometime after the 20th of August, and demands and requests from Vukovar to send for the organisers of a defence, I thought that he was the right man for the job.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you happen to know that just like you, he asked the JNA to relieve him of his duties in the JNA, or rather he deserted -- did he desert from the JNA? Do you know anything about that?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, he asked in writing to be let go from the JNA, for his service there to cease.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. I'd now like to ask you a couple of questions linked to a protected witness, so may we go into private session for a moment, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: At the time, did you also receive information -- I'm talking about the period when Dedakovic and Borkovic were on the territory of Vukovar. Did you receive from them information or hear about the fact that they had contacted my client through a Motorola and there are video recordings about that? Did you receive any information to that effect, that Sljivancanin appealed to them to surrender?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember exactly whether that was a contact with Sljivancanin himself, but that contacts of that kind during the war on the territory of Croatia, that is to say contacts through Motorolas, that is true, there were contacts of that nature.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Specifically, and I'm talking about the Vukovar events, did they inform you that the JNA representatives directly in the field were proposing an end to the fighting and surrender and cessation to any further military activities directly on the ground there in on the territory?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the time, when this came about, I no longer was in command of them on the -- in the sense of daily commanding, because I was engaged in negotiations with the JNA. At the time the daily contacts were maintained by the chief of the Main Staff of the Croatian army and his assistant, General Stipetic. What I do know is that there were certain stories along those lines, that there were proposals coming from the other side that they surrender.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Have you refreshed your memory perhaps? Do you remember receiving information from them about how many armoured JNA vehicles were destroyed or how many JNA members captured or how many soldiers were killed during the operations according to their information?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There was information to that effect, that a large number of armoured vehicles were destroyed. There was the Trpinska Cesta, that road, and that the adversary suffered heavy losses. There were figures which I don't recall at present. How far this was true, I don't know. How much it was bravado, I don't know. That's another matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I just asked you about the information, and I received my answer. Thank you. Now, do you know that during that time, and when I say that time, what I mean is the period of the Vukovar events themselves, October, November 1991, at that material time, that on the territory of Croatia there were JNA soldiers and officers who had been captured, captured in the true sense of the word, that were kept in detention in certain detention units?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I do know about that, that there were such people.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Was one of the tasks of the security organs in the unit to collect as much information as possible about soldiers who had disappeared, who had gone missing, soldiers from the unit or soldiers from another unit who had been captured by the other side? Is that one of the tasks of a security organ?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to the rules of service governing the certificate security services this is not mentioned as one of the specific tasks. However the security organ adjusting itself to the situation it finds itself in, may be assigned such a task or the organ can assess that they should be involved in a task of that kind. That is quite certain. That would be true, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: According to you, would you say that the JNA had the mandate and authority to liberate from prison either on the basis of an exchange, to get its soldiers and commanding officers back?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Each of the conflicting parties endeavours to do that, and JNA does so as well. And that's what the agreement signed on the 6th of March 1991 referred to. It referred to the exchange of prisoners.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The 6th of November 1991. Now, Mr. Borovic asked you something about the blockade of the barracks, and you said that one of the tasks of blocking the barracks was to control all incoming and outgoing traffic. Now, did the soldiers, JNA soldiers and commanding officers who were blocked in the Marshal Tito barracks, for example, in Zagreb, or in some other barracks that had also been blocked, were they able to enter and exit the barracks freely whilst they were under blockade up until the time they left the territory?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they were not able to enter and exit freely.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yesterday you mentioned a high-ranking officer of the garrison in Gospic who had been taken prisoner and detained by the Croatian side. Does Major Relja Tomic mean anything to you, the name?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not the man I had in mind. I don't remember that particular name and surname. I had in mind a Macedonian, in fact, I think he was a general. I don't know whether he was Macedonian but his surname ended in s-k-i, the letters s-k-i.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'll return to the subject of exchange of prisoners in a little while. But tell me this, please: In this courtroom we have heard that the commanders of the defence of Vukovar, Dedakovic and Borkovic, were later arrested and persecuted. Do you know anything about that and what the reasons for that were? Why proceedings were taken, I'll put it that way, why proceedings were taken against them?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that once they left Vukovar, and once Vukovar fell, that they were in a difficult situation, in disgrace, and the investigating organs of the military police investigated to see whether they had sabotaged the defence of Vukovar or whether they intentionally made the defence of Vukovar ineffective. I know, but I know this from the media, from the information media, that published news about that, and excerpts from the interviews conducted, that they asked about me too, whether I had not, as a former member of the security service taking part in a planned -- in making the defence of Vukovar ineffective, whether this -- I had taken part in the planning of that. However, that was a wartime situation. Everything happens in wars, and that is how I understood this particular episode as well. Later on, Borkovic and Dedakovic quite normally went about their service. Dedakovic actually retired and Dedakovic went on to do some more work.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What would your position be or attitude be and does that emanate from the answer you've just given us that Josip Manolic five days ago on Croatian television made a statement and said that he considers those two men to be deserters and traitors? So is that one of the lines that you spoke about and the policy towards these two individuals?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about that statement that you say Manolic made. However, I do know that Dedakovic and Borkovic did invest a great deal of effort to set up the defence and it is their merit to a great extent that the defence kept up for as long as it did. Now, how Manolic refers to them and what he calls them, perhaps he has some arguments to back up him doing so.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Who was Vinko Zunic?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. The name doesn't sound familiar.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In that same programme he was introduced as a commander of the defence of Bogdanovci and during that material time and he said that he left Bogdanovci on the 10th of November 1991. Is that roughly the period when Bogdanovci were left with what the man said? Does it sort of tally?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, the commander of Bogdanovci's defence was a certain man called -- well, he was called Lasta or swallow, Matkovic, and at the time, when I visited Bogdanovci, I was with him on that occasion. I think that was the 30th of September or -- yes, the 30th of September 1991, and that date does coincide with the time Bogdanovci fell.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I might pronounce the name wrongly again, but Tomislav Berhechter, does that ring a bell at all?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
